summary: A short note from Alex McKenzie at BBN that attaches network traffic statistics for the ARPANET for November 1972. The tables show how many packets each host sent over the period. It updates RFC 413. BBN had been giving these figures to ARPA each month and now shared them with the whole network community.

eli5.summary: This is a monthly tally from the early internet, showing how many packets each computer sent. Think of counting how many letters each house mailed in a month, so the post office can see where the traffic is.

questions: how much traffic did each arpanet host send
what is internode vs intranode traffic

subtitle: Packet counts for every ARPANET host in November 1972.

tldr.problem: Monthly traffic figures needed to be shared with the network community.
tldr.mechanism: The note attaches a Host Throughput Summary of packets output per host for November 1972, split into internode and intranode.
tldr.outcome: November totals were 24865310 internode and 5079571 intranode packets. The note updates RFC 413.

today: RFC 422 updates RFC 413 and has no recorded replacement. It is a historical snapshot of early ARPANET traffic.

sections.title: What Is Attached
sections.content: A. McKenzie of BBN attaches the host traffic statistics for November 1972, dated 11 December 1972. The note updates RFC 413, which carried the October figures.
sections.eli5: The next month's scoreboard, sent right after the last one.

sections.title: The Table
sections.content:
The Host Throughput Summary lists packets output by each host, with columns for internode packets, intranode packets, the total, the average daily internode figure and days counted. Most sites show 21 days.

Data is missing for days 1, 3, 4, 5, 17, 18, 19, 20 and 25. TINK and BELV had no traffic, and UCSD HOST 1 appears with a footnote marker [5].
sections.eli5: Each computer has a row of counts, and some days are missing from the tally.

sections.title: The Totals
sections.content: The November totals are 24865310 internode and 5079571 intranode packets. The daily averages are 1184062 and 241884, and the internode packets-to-messages ratio is 1.05.
sections.eli5: Adding every row gives how busy the whole network was that month.
